startup.name: Opusense AI
startup.description: Voice and photo capture for construction field inspectors that turns notes into a structured report on site. Two person team from Toronto with a civil engineering PhD and construction technology experience. Customers are inspection firms and contractors who pay to cut report writing time.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent third party range, references/yc_acceptance.md). Up for domain experience of 15 combined years and a PhD founder with a technical co founder (technical founder factor), and a clear daily pain with a measurable time saving. Neutral to down for a two person team with no stated revenue and a niche vertical. Net about 3 percent, and the forecast is conditional on acceptance as the batch is already given.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that field report writing for inspectors is a thin wedge with little evidence of paying customers, that several funded rivals already do voice and photo to report, and that Procore, Autodesk and Sitemate can add the same feature. With no stated revenue or pilots, partners may see a feature rather than a company.

anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 19.3 months from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17 and the probability is for a closed round above about 1M from outside investors inside that window, not ever. Anchor 0.59 B2B and 0.64 construction; 0.45 is 0.76x the B2B anchor. Most seed rounds for 2022 and later cohorts close by 14 months (p75), so a 19 month window captures most of the ever number, minus a niche discount. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round between 1M and 3M from angels and a pre seed fund; likely for a two person vertical team with domain credibility but early revenue. Excludes the standard 500K YC deal.
Typical institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of 4.1M in round_benchmarks, from a construction tech or vertical AI fund.
Strong seed if pilots with named inspection firms convert; 2026 raises above 1M had a quartile of 4.3M to 10M, but press leans large.
Rare large seed in construction tech for a two person team.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step above 1M fails if the two founders cannot show paying inspection firms inside a year, if investors judge voice to report a feature that Procore, Autodesk or Sitemate will ship, or if a better funded rival such as a competing voice inspection app wins the same firms. OSIMple (Winter 2018) built inspector software and stopped after a seed near 120 thousand dollars, and Machine26 and Feldy show construction wedges with no priced round found.

Typical Series A near the 2022 and later YC median of 14.15M (stage_benchmarks.md) and market deal size near 17M with pre money near 60M.
Upside round led by a top fund after clear revenue growth; the 2022 and later p75 is about 20M and hot AI categories exceed it.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A inside 19 months requires about 1M or more of monthly recurring revenue style traction in a slow adopting industry. Construction buyers sign long pilots and per seat prices are small, so growth is slow. Inspectify reached a Series A of 8M only after a seed and 12 months of strong sales, then cut staff in the housing slowdown, and OSIMple never passed seed.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C within 19 months of the start of YC is almost unheard of; it would require a company that has become the system of record for inspections across several countries, and no analog does. Most companies in the data take five years to reach C if they ever do.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company stalls as a two person tool with a few paying firms or is absorbed into a larger inspection or construction software suite for under 100M. Reaching a large exit needs the company to become the inspection workflow system, but incumbents with distribution and funded rivals take most of that value. OSIMple stalled after a small seed, Inspectify survived by acquisition and a smaller round, and Machine26 remains a small team.

analogs.relevance: Software for inspectors to automate paper workflow, same buyer.
analogs.outcome_summary: Shut down after a seed near 120K; shows thin inspector software markets.

analogs.relevance: Home inspection software with a seed then an 8M Series A.
analogs.outcome_summary: Series A in 2021, cut staff in 2022, kept going; shows vertical inspection can raise.
Active with no priced round found, a stall pattern.

analogs.relevance: Field capture and AI for home service contractors.
analogs.outcome_summary: Active, no priced round found, shows the field AI niche raises slowly.

killers.evidence: Procore, Autodesk and Sitemate already ship AI report drafting from voice and photos, and a web search of the market shows InspectMind and Property Inspect doing the same.
killers.mitigation: Pick one inspection type and integrate with the report formats firms already use.

killers.evidence: Construction is slow to adopt and inspection firms are small, so pilots may not convert to paid seats within a year.
killers.mitigation: Sell per report to larger firms and show a 5x time saving in writing.

killers.risk: Two person team and no stated revenue
killers.evidence: The input lists a team of 2 and no revenue figures, so investor trust depends on founder credibility only.
killers.mitigation: Add a third hire and get three paid pilots before raising.

killers.risk: Accuracy and liability of AI reports
killers.evidence: Inspection reports are legal documents; an error can create liability, which makes buyers insist on human review and slows adoption.
killers.mitigation: Keep a review step and an audit log.

technical_complexity.rationale: Speech to text, photo understanding and layout of structured reports are available from model providers. Hard parts are matching each firm report format and handling noisy site audio offline. A two person team can ship the core in months; the moat is formats and trust, not models.

takeover_risk.rationale: Existing platforms have inspection users and distribution and can add voice to report with off the shelf models in under a year. Funded rivals listed in the market search already do this.

evidence.claim: Vendors report that report writing takes a large share of inspector time, and several rivals now market the same saving.
A freelance marketplace lists custom builds of daily field report tools from voice and photos, showing demand for the workflow.

actions: Run paid pilots with three inspection firms
roadmap.proof: Three firms using it weekly and a measured saving.

roadmap.goal: Prove paid repeat usage in one inspection type.
actions: Price per report or per seat and convert pilots
Integrate with common report formats and project tools
roadmap.proof: At least 10 paying firms and recurring revenue growing monthly.

pros.evidence: Combined over 15 years in construction and a civil engineering PhD plus a startup engineer, per the application.
Report writing at about 20 percent of the week is a quantified time cost the founders claim to cut 5x.

brand.name: Opusense AI
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Opusense AI" --era 2022+: invented name, 8 characters, 3 syllables, no descriptor suffix.
strengths: The AI suffix signals the category
brand.rationale: An invented two part name is neutral. Many successful YC names are invented, but a name does not move construction buyers, who buy on workflow fit.

narrative.headline: A credible vertical AI wedge with real founder expertise, but a two person team in a feature crowded niche: about even odds of a 1M plus round inside 19 months.
narrative.general_summary: Opusense AI turns inspectors voice notes and photos into finished reports. The pain is real and quantified, and the founders know the buyer. The forecast window is 19.3 months from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17 and the seed number is for a round above about 1M closing inside it. The cohort anchor is about 59 percent ever, and the forecast sits slightly below it because the field is crowded with funded and incumbent products and the team is two people. Series A inside the window is unlikely because it takes a median 28 months. The odds here do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast as of 2025-04-07 using only the provided input, which gives no revenue or customer counts.
Seed means a round above about 1M from outside investors inside the 19.3 month window, not the 500K YC deal.
Funding data for the cohorts is partial, so lower and upper bounds were used.
